basis: Press names the firm in the company's rounds: TechCrunch (2023-09-26) reports Series 'backed by $25 million in funding across seed and Series A rounds led by 776 and Basis Set Ventures, with participation from Pear VC, Kleiner Perkins, Day One Ventures' and others. The co-founder's earlier job at Kleiner Perkins is named separately, so the firm is in as an investor (decisions.md R1: press naming Kleiner Perkins in a round).

note: Finance and operations software meant to replace ERP systems, San Francisco (TechCrunch, 2023-09-26). The one report gives $25M across a seed and a Series A with Kleiner Perkins among the participants and does not say which round the firm entered, so the stage is undetermined. Status unknown: the company's domain (seriesfi.com, the address TechCrunch links) lapsed in September 2026 and serves the registrar's expiry page, and no report of a shutdown, a sale or a later round was found. Momentum check 2026-09-30: no priced round at $1B or more (one web search and TechCrunch's own search, which holds only the 2023 report).

funding_rounds.round: Seed and Series A ($25M total, announced together)

basis: The firm is a selling holder on a filed agreement: the Share Purchase Agreement of 2002-07-24 by which Liberate Technologies bought Sigma Systems Group (Canada) Inc. is signed 'KLEINER PERKINS CAUFIELD & BYERS By: Raymond Lane, Partner' among 'the holders listed on the signature pages', beside Redwood Ventures IV and Morgan Stanley (the filing names the firm, not a numbered fund). Lexpert corroborates the round: US$20M announced 2000-08-22, 'led by Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers ... and Redwood Ventures'. The member is Sigma, not Liberate (decisions.md R5).

note: Service provisioning software for cable broadband operators, Toronto (the agreement gives the company's address as 55 York Street, Toronto; an Ontario corporation). Bought by Liberate Technologies under the share purchase agreement of 2002-07-24. The firm entered in the US$20M round of August 2000, which Lexpert calls 'the first round of financing' of a company founded in 1990: a description, not a round name, so the stage is undetermined.

funding_rounds.lead: Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers; Redwood Ventures

basis: Press names the firm in the seed: UK Tech Investment News (2019-09-25) reports Skew 'has raised $2 million in seed funding from several venture capital firms, including Silicon Valley icon Kleiner Perkins', led by firstminute capital with Seedcamp, Kima Ventures and QCP Capital; CoinDesk (2020-04-29) repeats that the 2019 seed was backed by Kleiner Perkins.

note: Crypto derivatives data and analytics, London; bought by Coinbase (announced April 2021), as the Seedcamp row reads. S2A: graduated on the step-up rule. The $2M seed of September 2019 was followed by a $5M round led by Octopus Ventures on 2020-04-29 (CoinDesk; City A.M. and Octopus's own post agree), which no press report read names a Series A, and $5M meets max(2x the $2M seed, $5M). The Seedcamp row reads not graduated on the Coinbase sale and does not record this round.

basis: A filing names the firm's funds as holders: the Spectrum HoloByte (MicroProse) proxy of 1996-07-29 footnotes Vinod Khosla's line with '648,172 shares of Common Stock held by Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers VI; 80,197 shares of Common Stock held by KPCB VI Founders Fund', and says he has been a director 'of Spectrum HoloByte since its inception in September 1992' (decisions.md D1, R6: the footnote names the fund). The position was taken in the private company in 1992, before the merger with the listed MicroProse in 1993 (D4).

note: Video game developer and publisher (Falcon, Tetris), Alameda. The firm's funds came in when the company was reorganized in September 1992 and bought back the shares Robert Maxwell's companies had held (Wikipedia; the 1996 proxy dates Vinod Khosla's seat to that inception); no source names the round, so the stage is undetermined. Status disputes the prefilled defunct: the company merged with MicroProse in 1993, took its name in 1996 and was bought by Hasbro Interactive in 1998 (Wikipedia), so it reads acquired; the Alameda studio was closed a year later.

funding_rounds.round: investment at the September 1992 reorganization (not named)

basis: Press names the firm among the company's investors: TechCrunch (2026-02-06) writes 'Terradot's investor list includes Gigascale Capital, Google, Kleiner Perkins, and Microsoft', and the December 2024 funding reports (Pulse 2.0, 2024-12-18) list Kleiner Perkins among the venture funds in the $58.2M raised, apart from John Doerr, who led as an individual (decisions.md R1; R4 keeps the partner's own money out, the fund is named separately). The firm's own site does not list the company.

note: Carbon removal by enhanced rock weathering, founded at Stanford in 2022, California-based with operations in Brazil; it bought its competitor Eion in February 2026 (TechCrunch). The December 2024 reports give $58.2M as a $4.2M seed plus a $54M Series A and list the investors of both together (lead John Doerr; venture funds Floodgate, Kleiner Perkins, Acre, Gigascale, Valor, Ponderosa), so the round the firm entered is not on record and the stage is undetermined. A vendor profile (Preqin, not cited) calls the Series A led by Kleiner Perkins; a release that separates the rounds would settle it as Series A.

basis: A company-side source and press name the firm in the first round: the founding team's timeline (totalentertainment.fyi) records for 1995 'Kleiner Perkins makes the initial investment', and Wikipedia cites the Business Wire release of 1995-04-24, 'Planet Optigon, Outland to merge and form The Total Entertainment Network; ... receive venture financing from Kleiner Perkins, Caulfield & Byers'. Wikipedia also reports the firm's own 1999 consumer-media portfolio page listing the company; that capture was not read (the Internet Archive is in the machine-wide cooldown), so the verdict rests on the round, not on the listing.

note: Online game network formed in 1995 from Optigon Interactive and Outland, San Francisco; renamed Pogo.com in 1999 and bought by Electronic Arts in 2001 (Wikipedia). The firm made the initial investment at the 1995 merger (Vinod Khosla), which the sources call the first round of venture financing without a round name, so the stage is undetermined; a round of more than $12M led by Vertex, Goldman Sachs and Ameritech followed in February 1996.

basis: Press names the firm in two rounds: InternetNews (1999-12-14) reports that 'both Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers and Sequoia Capital invested in the company's second round of venture financing', $12.5M led by Sequoia, 'and this marks Kleiner Perkins' second investment in the company', with partner Russ Siegelman joining the board. The Keynote merger agreement of 2004-09-10 then gives 'Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers (KPCB)' and Partech consent rights over the shareholders' representative (the firm, not a person: decisions.md R1, R2).

note: Web customer experience research, San Mateo; merged into Keynote Systems under the agreement of 2004-09-10. The December 1999 report calls the $12.5M Sequoia-led round the firm's second investment and puts total funding at $18M, so the firm entered in an earlier round that no source read names or dates: the stage is undetermined and no entry date is given.

The firm entered in the seed TechCrunch reported on 2012-04-04 with North Bridge and Cue Ball; the company's one Form D shows that round selling from July 2011 ($1.0M of $1.25M by November 2011), and the entry is dated by the announcement because no source dates the firm's own check. basis: Name match only (decisions.md R1): the basis is a Komag officer's biography calling Zambeel 'a Kleiner/ Perkins and NEA storage startup', and Juniper's April 2002 proxy adds Vinod Khosla's seat on Zambeel's board, both person-level lines in third parties' filings. No fund of the firm is named on a filing (Zambeel's one filing is a paper REGDEX of 2003), the firm's listing was not found, and no press or company source naming Kleiner Perkins in a Zambeel round could be read: the two pages a web search returned for it (Network Computing, StorageSearch) no longer resolve and the rest are vendor profiles. Without the corroboration R1 asks for the candidate is not added; the firm's 2001-03 archived listing or one readable round report would reverse this.
